title: THE MARY CELESTE | Part 3: What Happened?
description:
Pirates, sea monsters, alcohol fumes, a broken pump. After 150 years, what really happened to the ten people on the Mary Celeste? The final part.

Part 3 (final) of an animated mystery series about the Mary Celeste. Tell us your theory in the comments.

series.name: The Mary Celeste
series.previously: The Mary Celeste was found drifting with no one on board. A court in Gibraltar found no evidence of a crime. So why would ten people leave a seaworthy ship in the middle of the ocean?

shots.say: For more than a hundred and fifty years, people have suggested every explanation imaginable. Pirates. Giant waves. Sea monsters. Even aliens.
But pirates would have taken the cargo and the valuables. And they were still on board.
There was one strange clue. When the cargo was unloaded in Genoa, nine of the barrels were empty. They were made of red oak, a more porous wood, and may have leaked.
shots.caption: 9 EMPTY BARRELS.

shots.say: One theory says alcohol fumes built up in the closed hold. Maybe there was a rumble, a strong smell, or a small burst of vapor.
Afraid the cargo might explode, Captain Briggs may have ordered everyone into the lifeboat. That could explain why the hatch was found open.
shots.caption: ABANDON SHIP?

shots.say: Another clue: one of the ship's pumps had been taken apart. Maybe the crew believed the ship was taking on water faster than it really was.
And land was close. The island of Santa Maria was in sight. A short trip in a small boat must have seemed safe.
Many researchers believe they planned to stay close, maybe tied to the ship by a line, and wait to see what happened.
But if that line broke, or the wind rose, the ship would sail away on her own. And a tiny boat would be left alone in the open Atlantic.
shots.caption: ALONE.

shots.say: No trace of the ten people, or the lifeboat, was ever found.
As for the Mary Celeste, she sailed for twelve more years. Sailors called her unlucky.
In eighteen eighty-five, her last captain deliberately ran her onto a reef off the coast of Haiti, to collect the insurance money. The fraud was discovered.
Benjamin Briggs, his wife Sarah, little Sophia, and their seven crewmen were never seen again.
So what do you think happened on the Mary Celeste? Tell me your theory in the comments.
